# The hardness gate

Canonical source: `../hardness-laws.md`. Derived over seven printed-optimum
tasks (four measured pass@5 clears, three withdrawn on probe). Read its "Honest
limits" section before treating any of this as certainty — at n=5 against a 60%
bar, a genuinely 70%-fail design still misses the gate ~16% of the time.

## The law

> Ship only if, with **every stated rule held correctly**, a competent solver still
> cannot cheaply *construct* the optimum. That requires **≥2 load-bearing beliefs**
> that are misreadable, narrowing, public-blind, unrepairable by restart, and
> **silent** under the printed optimum, plus **one stated resource constraint** that
> makes the bulk/uniform architecture illegal.

Whether a belief is stated in one sentence or entailed across sections is
irrelevant — that axis is dead. State everything. A stated rule is worth exactly
what its measured wrong-belief rate says.

## Why those conditions and not others

The agent's cheapest winning strategy is *transcribe → simulate → over-enumerate →
check against N*. Each condition closes one leg of it:

- **A transcribed simulator enforces per-step legality for free.** So any fact
  entailed by step legality is worth zero — the simulator rejects violations
  without ever deriving the fact. Difficulty can only live in facts needed to
  *emit* a candidate: whole-plan or terminal properties, or the identity/layout of
  the objects acted on. **Constructive, not checkable.**
- **A printed optimum is a free belief oracle on sealed data.** `cost == N` runs
  inside the graded program with no feedback channel. A wrong belief that
  overshoots, undershoots, wedges, crashes or exhausts a resource is an *alarm*,
  and one retry repairs it. Only beliefs whose wrong plans self-report
  `cost == N, all checks pass` survive.
- **Restart repairs every over-permissive slip.** It cannot cross an action-space
  boundary. Measured: one slot's over-permissive seal-blind was restarted
  around 12/12; its narrowing freeze-blind killed 9/12 and was unrepairable.

The whole gate is the conjunction: **narrowing enough that search cannot cross,
silent enough that the agent never learns to search again.**

## Pre-build check — run before writing task files

Steps 1–4 are paper. Steps 5–9 need only the reference solver and one-line
mutations of it. Do not start building until step 9 passes.

1. **Write the reference solver first.** Annotate every design decision with the
   rule that forces it.
2. **Enumerate load-bearing beliefs.** Keep only facts F where a solver holding ¬F
   cannot produce a correct answer on some instance — ¬F must change the legal-move
   set or the identity of the objects acted on. **Discard representation and
   memoisation facts**; they change tractability, not legality.
3. **Constructive or checkable?** If F is entailed by per-step legality, a
   transcribed simulator gets it free — worth zero. Keep only whole-plan/terminal
   properties and object identity.
4. **Rank by misreadability.** The deciding rule must fire *often in the answer*
   while being *easy to over-read*.
5. **Public-blindness, by execution.** Each ¬F solver must **PASS** the public /
   worked case, 1/1. No numeric worked example may instantiate F. Kill any ¬F that
   fails public.
6. **Sealed kill rate.** Each ¬F, with search left perfect, must fail **≥1/3 of
   sealed instances** (≥4 of 12). Below that, drop the belief.
7. **Restart-proof.** Run each ¬F under its own belief with 10⁴ restarts or 100×
   oracle time per instance, whichever is larger. Require **0 solves** on its
   failing instances. Expect half your candidates to die here.
8. **N-silence — the condition everyone skips.** On the sealed instances it fails,
   each ¬F must terminate and self-report `cost == N`, end state legal, own
   validator green, on **≥2/3 of them**. If it crashes, wedges, exhausts a resource
   or overshoots N on more than 1/3, it is a klaxon and one retry repairs it —
   score it zero.
9. **Gate.** ≥2 beliefs surviving 5–8; ≥3 independent failure classes with
   near-disjoint failing-instance sets (pairwise Jaccard < 0.5); and 1 stated
   resource constraint verified by implementing the uncurated bulk architecture
   (stage/copy/enumerate everything) and confirming it fails **100% of sealed**.

## Strong probe — diagnostic, runs last

Implement, as the adversary would: correct rules transcribed into a faithful
simulator; action alphabet = verbs × the full named ground set, **uncurated,
including every reserved or auxiliary name the spec mentions**; randomised greedy
with restart plus unpruned DFS with `seen` memoisation; accept iff end state
matches and `cost == N`; on repeated wedge, flip one bit in a 2–4 element belief
lattice. Run under the real per-item cap, with `n_items × cap < verifier
timeout_sec` and cap ≈ 100× oracle cost.

Report solves/sealed, wall time per instance, feasible fraction, cost per candidate
test.

- Probe solves ≥8/12 within 10% of cap **and** <2 beliefs surviving step 8 →
  **dead, do not build.**
- Probe solves but ≥2 surviving beliefs and the resource constraint → **ship.** A
  dead search space is the normal state of a good design.
- **Density below ~1e-7 only**, and only as `expected_draws × cost_per_draw > 10 ×
  cap`. The band 1e-4 to 1e-1 is worth exactly zero — measured on all three
  withdrawn designs. Never make tightness the sole defence.

## Two standing tripwires

- Never ship an object the solver should derive (a shipped entity map killed
  an exploratory-data-analysis slot).
- Never write a sentence that performs the derivation: *"order makes no
  difference"*, *"any schedule meeting these conditions is accepted"*, or a printed
  formula whose state-valued reading is the pruning heuristic.

## Where to spend the budget

**Stop spending it on scheduling order.** Ordering is always cheap, always
restart-repairable, always audited by N. Spend it on (i) what the objects *are* —
layouts composed from stated formulas, index maps, padding on padding — and (ii) a
stated scarce resource that outlaws the bulk architecture. Those are the two legs
every survivor stands on.

The shape's expiry is **similarity**, not difficulty: three same-author
printed-optimum tasks came back UNIQUE; a fourth or fifth will not. The untried
successor axis is **making a single candidate test expensive** — feasibility of one
move requires solving a nested subproblem, so `cost == N` cannot be evaluated
cheaply and the simulator-as-filter stops being free.
